title: Terminal and Orbit Anew
premise: Bram Delacroix, an insurance investigator sent to assess the 'impossible' accidents aboard the failing colony station Terminal, discovers the disasters are deliberate sabotage by a faction of colonists who want the reactor's countdown stopped and half of humanity's cryopods preserved for a future that may never come. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, Bram realizes the signal is coming from within the station itself — from pods holding the last speakers of Old Meridian, the culture both factions descend from. As the reactor's countdown accelerates, Bram must choose which half of humanity wakes: the saboteurs' chosen heirs or the forgotten founders. In the end, Bram wakes neither faction intact but a mixed crew of both — including their own estranged sibling, asleep for forty years — and together they abandon Terminal for an orbital ark called Orbit Anew, carrying the language, the memories, and the found family they built in the dark.
about_author: Bram Coldharbour is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the people who keep records when no one else will.

chapters.title: The Adjuster Arrives
chapters.summary: Bram Delacroix docks at Terminal station to investigate three impossible accidents, armed with forms and professional detachment. Through Bram's POV, we see a colony of two hundred pretending everything is fine while lights flicker and corridors go cold. The emotional beat is wary loneliness: Bram has been sent to price a death everyone else has already accepted.

chapters.title: Inventory of Small Disasters
chapters.summary: Bram interviews survivors and catalogs the accidents: a coolant breach, a collapsed hydroponics bay, a decompression that killed no one but erased the station's seed archive. POV shifts between Bram and station archivist Yara Osei, who keeps her own unauthorized records. The beat is quiet dread as Bram notices the accidents share a signature no machine could leave.

chapters.title: Paperwork for the End of the World
chapters.summary: Bram files preliminary findings suggesting human sabotage, knowing the insurance payout will trigger evacuation — and abandonment — of Terminal. Yara shows Bram the cryobay: four hundred pods, half labeled with names, half with only serial numbers. The beat is moral unease; Bram's report will decide who gets remembered.

chapters.title: The Language That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: A distress signal arrives on a dead frequency, spoken in Old Meridian, a language extinct since Earth's Second Consolidation. Yara recognizes fragments; her grandmother sang them. Bram, whose family buried the language after their parents emigrated, understands every word. The beat is vertigo: the past is calling from inside the station.

chapters.title: Serial Numbers Have Faces
chapters.summary: Bram traces the signal to the unlabeled pods and discovers they hold the Founders' Circle — the original colonists, asleep for eighty years, written out of official history by the current administration. POV alternates with Administrator Voss, who knows exactly what's in those pods. The beat is betrayal: the colony was built on an erasure.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Remembers
chapters.summary: Bram inspects the reactor and finds the countdown isn't a malfunction — it's a scheduled shutdown coded by the Founders themselves, meant to force a choice about who wakes. Voss's faction wants to override it and wake their own people first. The beat is rising tension as Bram realizes the sabotage and the countdown are two hands of the same clock.

chapters.title: Yara's Grandmother Sings
chapters.summary: Yara plays Bram a recording of lullabies in Old Meridian, and Bram finally speaks the language aloud for the first time since childhood, grieving a parent who forbade it. The two form a fragile alliance over shared inheritance. The beat is tenderness: memory as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: Sabotage, Fourth Incident
chapters.summary: A fourth accident nearly kills Bram: an airlock cycles early, and only Yara's warning saves them. Bram confronts Voss, who denies involvement but reveals the saboteurs call themselves the Heirs — colonists who believe waking the Founders means surrendering the future to ghosts. The beat is fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Heirs' Manifesto
chapters.summary: Bram finds the Heirs' manifesto hidden in maintenance logs: they've been sabotaging the station to accelerate the crisis, forcing an early vote on which pods open. Their leader is revealed to be Dr. Imre Delacroix — Bram's sibling, missing for forty years. The beat is a gut-punch of personal stakes colliding with political ones.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: In flashback chapters woven through Bram's investigation, we learn Imre chose cryosleep after their parents' death, refusing to live in a colony that erased their heritage. Bram stayed awake and forgot. The beat is sorrowful recognition: Bram and Imre made opposite choices from the same wound.

chapters.title: Countdown Acceleration
chapters.summary: The Heirs' latest sabotage cracks the reactor containment; the countdown drops from months to nineteen days. Voss declares martial law and moves to seize the cryobay. Bram must choose sides publicly or lose access to everything. The beat is the point of no return.

chapters.title: A Vote Nobody Called
chapters.summary: Yara organizes the unaligned colonists — neither Heirs nor administration loyalists — into a third faction demanding the vote include the Founders' own recorded wishes. Bram testifies, translating Old Meridian testimony from the pods' pre-sleep messages. The beat is cautious hope: democracy attempted under deadline.

chapters.title: Voss's Countermove
chapters.summary: Voss reveals she's decoded the Founders' messages too — and one of them authorizes her to decide alone if consensus fails. She begins selective thawing of loyalist pods. Bram realizes the investigation that brought them here was commissioned by Voss to legitimize exactly this. The beat is fury and disillusionment.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Cryobay
chapters.summary: Bram, Yara, and a handful of colonists physically occupy the cryobay to stop Voss's selective thawing. Imre arrives with the Heirs — not to fight, but because the manifesto's final clause requires a Delacroix witness for any pod opening. The beat is tense standoff, siblings face to face across forty years.

chapters.title: The Founders' Real Message
chapters.summary: With Imre's help, Bram fully translates the Founders' final recording: they never intended either faction to win. The countdown was designed so the reactor fails unless pods from both lists open together — a technical inheritance lock. The beat is revelation reframing the whole conflict: survival was always conditional on reconciliation.

chapters.title: Nineteen Becomes Nine
chapters.summary: Further sabotage — this time by a Voss loyalist acting alone — accelerates the countdown to nine days. Evacuation ships can reach only half the colonists. Panic spreads; Yara's archive becomes the station's de facto town hall. The beat is desperation forging unlikely community.

chapters.title: Orbit Anew
chapters.summary: Yara uncovers blueprints in the Founder archives for Orbit Anew, an unfinished orbital ark designed to carry a mixed complement to a nearby moon. It needs a reactor core — and Terminal's dying reactor can be cannibalized if someone stays behind to manage the extraction. The beat is hope with a terrible price attached.

chapters.title: Who Stays
chapters.summary: The colonists debate who remains to run the extraction: a suicide-adjacent posting. Voss volunteers, seeking redemption, and asks Bram to witness her decision in writing — the investigator's final report becoming something closer to a eulogy. The beat is grace arriving through the least likely person.

chapters.title: Thawing Both Halves
chapters.summary: With nine days left, the station executes the joint thawing protocol: Founders and Heirs' chosen wake together, disoriented, angry, and alive. Bram mediates the first meeting between Imre and the Founders who signed away their era. The beat is painful, necessary confrontation — inheritance claimed rather than received.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: The reactor core transfer begins under Voss's hands while Terminal shakes itself apart. Bram coordinates the evacuation, translating between factions in real time as Old Meridian becomes the working language of the operation. The beat is kinetic unity: a colony finally moving in the same direction.

chapters.title: The Last Report
chapters.summary: From Orbit Anew's observation deck, Bram watches Terminal go dark and files the true final report — not an assessment of loss, but a record of who woke, who stayed, and why. Voss's last transmission confirms the extraction succeeded. The beat is elegiac closure: paperwork as love letter.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the ark's first assembly gathers — Founders, Heirs, and the unaligned, teaching each other songs and systems. Bram and Imre plant the recovered seeds from Yara's backup archive. The beat is quiet renewal: a found family inheriting a future they built together from the wreckage of forgetting.
